title: Could use a little feedback on the game I’m working on.
author: blackwidowink
selftext:
Hey guys,

I’ve been working on this endless dungeon runner for a while and I’m reaching a point where I have a few more plans of things to add, but I could really use a little bit of feedback to keep me focused. 

Coding is done by Claude and the LK game engine. Adventurer sprites are by ‘rvros’ and monster sprites by ‘LuizMelo’, both on itch.io. Everything else was generated by either LK game engine or ChatGPT 4o. Music by Riffusion. 

If you wouldn’t mind checking it out and some constructive criticism my way, that would be much appreciated. 

Can be played [here](https://upit.com/@blackwidowink/play/_CK2GYKD5Y)

comments.author: MultiKausal
comments.body: Really cool. Which platform are you planning to release? I would like to play this as a casual mobile i guess 🔥✌🏼

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Thanks! This one was just a learning experience for me. The platform it’s on is where it will live most likely. It’s definitely a mobile game, as the controls are all geared towards touch screen.

comments.author: CanyonClapper
comments.body: I really like the music and the fact that you can dash makes the movement and fighting cool af

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Thanks! Yeah I think the fun factor jumped up when I added the dash and ground slam, personally.

comments.author: natandestroyer
comments.body: What is the LK game engine?

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: It’s a AI powered JavaScript game engine. Can find it at Upit.com. Still in beta.

comments.author: cameruso
comments.body: Very slick indeed. Had a little play, though on laptop w mouse, sweet little game!

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Thanks! I’m sorry I couldn’t give you better controls. The engine doesn’t allow for keyboard access yet.

replies.author: cameruso
replies.body: Not at all. Do you have a link to the engine?

comments.author: officialraylong
comments.body: To make this pop, you should add a bit of blur to the background assets. The farther away something is, the less detailed it looks (hence, LOD in 3d games - no need to render details that shouldn't be seen). The topmost layer of the parallax scrolling could be darker, more desaturated than the middle layers. Hollow Knight makes excellent use of this in 2.5D parallax scrolling. Lastly, sprites and game objects should contrast with the environment so that the eye easily reads them. If the climate is cold, make the sprite warm. If the environment is warm, make the sprites cooler on the color wheel.

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Great feedback. Thanks! I’m planning a graphical overhaul to match pixel counts a bit better as well. Appreciate you.

replies.author: officialraylong
replies.body: I'm happy to help! A neat trick on the color wheel is to start at your current color and walk a counterclockwise spiral out to the edge. You'll get a nice chromatic shift. For example, you can use dark purple in shadows for green sprites highlighted with a yellow edge.

comments.author: blindgoatia
comments.body: The player sprite looks identical to what’s in Idle Slayer

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: It’s the same one actually. I got it from an artist named ‘rvros’ on itch.io before I had even heard of Idle Slayer. I’m going to bet the Idle Slayer dev got it from the same place.

replies.author: blindgoatia
replies.body: Crazy! Cool stuff. Game looks good!

comments.author: zerossoul
comments.body: It feels slow. Which is odd because some actions like jumping feel fast.

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Ive actually sped up the running animation speed a bit since making that video. I think that’s what you’re feeling.

comments.author: Individual_Record521
comments.body: That player model is one of the most used assets, I'd recommend a different one

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Appreciate the advice, but this is just a hobby game. If I planned on releasing it commercially I’d switch over.

replies.author: Individual_Record521
replies.body: Makes perfect sense, how do you find the work flow for the engine you're using. I've been using Rosebud

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Personally, I love it. Getting better all the time.

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Thanks very much, I appreciate that.

comments.author: Canary_Earth
comments.body: Realms of Chaos is so good! Make your bats faster. They should be the most annoying enemy in the game.

comments.author: stuffedcrust_studios
comments.body:
hard to say without playing myself but as someone else said it does feel a bit slow, i guess just the player run speed needs increasing.

also it feels a bit weird in the 4:3 aspect ratio or whatever it is, would be better if it was widescreen and the player was a bit less so far left on the screen? or if there was a bit more play in the camera focus, like when you dash the camera rigidly sticks to the player but maybe when you dash you should move forwards on the screen and then the camera kinda catches up? might make it feel a bit more dynamic.

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback! I’ve sped up all animation speeds since I posted this and it feels a lot better. 

The aspect ratio is what I’m stuck with on the platform that I’m building on. I’ve asked for options, but so far not implemented. 

As for the dash, because it’s an endless runner I elected to not change the player’s horizontal position at all and the movement is just everything else in the game moving around them. You are the second one to mention the dash, however, so I will take another look! Thank you!

comments.author: isamuelcrozier
comments.body:
Good obstacles. Good visuals. Looks sloggish. 

The scrolling movement looks slow, like you as the developer are hovering over me as the player and smiling as you introduce me to the uncanny valley.

I'm bored from here, and that's recognizing that you offered me a toolkit that looks snappy.

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body: Appreciate it. I have increased animation speeds since posting this, so maybe that has alleviated the feeling of sluggishness that you were feeling a bit. Thanks for taking the time.
